wu: Plan Pictionary: Write weekend plans on slips (e.g., 'visit grandma', 'study English'). Students draw; classmates guess using 'Are you going to...?' and the drawer responds 'Yes, I am.' or 'No, I'm going to...'.
wuAlt: Plan Charades: Act out holiday plans; peers guess with 'Are you going to...?'
Plan Relay: Teams race to write 'going to' sentences about their weekend on the board.
pres: Show flashcards of Moroccan holidays (Eid, Green March). Model: 'For Eid, I'm going to visit my family after I pray.' Elicit similar sentences. Check with thumbs-up/down: 'Are you going to...?'
presAlt: Use a calendar with events; ask 'What are you going to do on...?'
Show a video of a local festival; pause to ask 'What are they going to do next?'
prac: Find Someone Who...: Students mingle, ask 'Are you going to... this weekend?', write names. Review with 'Yes, [name] is going to...' or 'No, but [name] is going to...'.
pracAlt: Plan Dominoes: Match 'going to' phrases with time clauses (e.g., 'after school' + 'do homework').
Plan Bingo: Call out plans; students cover if they match their own.
ls: Listen to a teen's holiday plans (audio). Students tick activities heard and underline 'going to + when' phrases. Check answers in pairs.
re: Plan Freeze: Teacher calls a plan (e.g., 'going to the beach'); students mime it. On 'Freeze!', they freeze and say a sentence (e.g., 'I'm going to swim after I eat lunch').
prod: Two-Corner Debate: Divide class into 'City Holiday' vs. 'Beach Holiday'. Groups prepare 3 reasons using 'going to + when'. Present; peers ask follow-up questions ('When are you going to leave?').
rw: Read a short text about a teen's Green March plans. Underline all 'going to' + time clauses. Write 3 similar sentences about their own Independence Day plans.
st: Sing 'What Are You Going to Do?' (to the tune of 'Frère Jacques'). Close with: 'Today we talked about plans using going to. Thank you, class!'
g: Draw weekend plans; guess with 'Are you going to...?'
Teams race to write 'going to' sentences on the board
Mingle and ask about weekend plans
Mime plans and say sentences on 'Freeze'
Argue for city vs. beach holiday plans
diff: Fast finishers: Write a paragraph about a dream holiday using 3 'going to + when' clauses.
Support: Use sentence starters like 'I'm going to... after I...'.
hw: Complete the future plans worksheet from the library folder.
Write 5 sentences about your Labour Day plans using 'going to + when'.
Interview a family member about their weekend plans and report back.
tip: Use local holidays (Eid, Green March) to make plans relatable; teens engage more when discussing familiar events.
